title: The holy city comes down
hookLine: not escape to the clouds, but heaven and earth renewed
carry: heaven comes down to make creation new

lines: A MAN ON A CLOUD WITH A HARP.
cards: A cartoon in a magazine: a man in a white robe sits alone on a cloud, holding a harp, looking bored. The joke works because the picture is familiar.

Heaven, in it, is somewhere up and away, thin and misty, where souls float off once the body is done, and the earth is left behind like an old coat. Now open the last pages of the Bible and watch which way things move.
John doesn't see anyone floating up. He sees something coming down.

teach.b: First, the direction. John writes: "And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven." Down.
God's home arrives on earth, and a voice says "the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them." The ending isn't people leaving the world. It's God moving in.
Second, the prayer Christians already pray.

teach.h: IN EARTH, AS IT IS IN HEAVEN.
teach.b: In the Lord's Prayer, Jesus teaches, "Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven." Not take us out of the earth; bring heaven's way into it.

Third, creation waiting. Paul writes to Rome that "the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now," and hopes that "the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption."
Not only people: the whole created world, waiting to be set free. Isaiah had said it long before: "For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth." Fourth, the word.
A couple of weeks ago this block heard Paul say that anyone in Christ "is a new creature." The Greek behind that, kainē ktisis, can just as well be translated new creation.
The same hope runs from one person to the whole world: not thrown away, made new. Christians hold these pictures in different balances. Some speak mostly of heaven as where the faithful go at death.
Others stress that God will renew this earth itself. Some hold both: rest with God now, and a renewed creation at the end. What the Bible's last pages add is the direction.

how: Christians pray "thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven" in the Lord's Prayer, and some churches link the hope of a new creation with caring for the earth, through creation-care ministries or a season of prayer for creation.

o: the creation story told at the start of Genesis
God making the whole world new, not throwing it away
a newly founded church starting from scratch

games.q: heaven comes down — tap the pairs.
p: coming down from God out of heaven
in earth, as it is in heaven
new heavens and a new earth

s: in Revelation, the faithful float up to a city in the clouds
John sees the holy city coming down from God out of heaven.
Paul hopes creation itself will be set free, not only people
"the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption."
all Christians picture heaven the same way
some speak mostly of heaven at death, some stress a renewed earth, and some hold both.

games.q: you're John, near the end of your vision. the holy city, new Jerusalem, appears. which way is it moving?
o: rising up, away from the earth.
coming down from God out of heaven.
hanging still, far off in the sky.
games.why: "coming down from God out of heaven." and a voice says God will dwell with them. the ending isn't escape; it's God moving in.

practice: Notice what's right around you: the floor under your feet, the air, a plant, the view through a window. In this hope, all of it is worth making new, not throwing away.
If you pray, you can say the line from the Lord's Prayer, thy will be done in earth; if not, just let your attention rest on the ground under you.

wordCard.voice: New creation. The hope that God doesn't throw the world away but makes it new, heaven and earth renewed, God dwelling with people.

orig.note: Greek: new creation, or new creature, Paul's phrase in 2 Corinthians 5:17.

carryVoice: Your line: heaven comes down to make creation new. This earth isn't an old coat to leave behind. See you tomorrow.
